subject: WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative / dealing with empirical underidentification

messages.author: ebad7f3c1ac5f1e2
messages.subject: WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative / dealing with empirical underidentification
parts:
Dear all,

I'm relatively new to lavaan and would greatly appreciate some advice on the following issue.
I ran a cfa model as follows:

# I use ordinal variables in Likert-scale lacking multivariate normal distribution - ordered and resulting robust estimation methods are recommended for such cases
# Define ordered(c(...)) as input for cfa
STP.data[,c("CEM_Phil_1","CEM_Phil_2","CEM_Phil_3","CEM_Pol_1","CEM_Pol_2","CEM_Pol_3","CEM_Pol_4","CEM_Pol_5","CEM_Pract_1","CEM_Pract_2","CEM_Pract_3","CEM_Pract_4","CEM_Proc_1","CEM_Proc_2","CEM_Proc_PS_1","CEM_Proc_PS_2","CEM_Proc_HR_2","CEM_Proc_HR_3","CEM_Proc_OP_1","CEM_Proc_OP_2")] <- lapply(STP.data[,c("CEM_Phil_1","CEM_Phil_2","CEM_Phil_3","CEM_Pol_1","CEM_Pol_2","CEM_Pol_3","CEM_Pol_4","CEM_Pol_5","CEM_Pract_1","CEM_Pract_2","CEM_Pract_3","CEM_Pract_4","CEM_Proc_1","CEM_Proc_2","CEM_Proc_PS_1","CEM_Proc_PS_2","CEM_Proc_HR_2","CEM_Proc_HR_3","CEM_Proc_OP_1","CEM_Proc_OP_2")], ordered)

# Define model, four-factor model with correlated factors, two variables (CEM_Proc_OP_1 and CEM_Proc_OP_2) freed to "load" on CEM_Proc and CEM_Pract
Four.factor.multiple <- '
CEM_Phil =~ CEM_Phil_1 + CEM_Phil_2 + CEM_Phil_3
CEM_Pol =~ CEM_Pol_1 + CEM_Pol_2 + CEM_Pol_3 + CEM_Pol_4 + CEM_Pol_5
CEM_Pract =~ CEM_Pract_1 + CEM_Pract_2 + CEM_Pract_3 + CEM_Pract_4 + CEM_Proc_OP_1 + CEM_Proc_OP_2
CEM_Proc =~ CEM_Proc_1 + CEM_Proc_2 + CEM_Proc_PS_1 + CEM_Proc_PS_2 + CEM_Proc_HR_2 + CEM_Proc_HR_3 + CEM_Proc_OP_1 + CEM_Proc_OP_2
CEM_Phil ~~ CEM_Pol
CEM_Phil ~~ CEM_Pract
CEM_Phil ~~ CEM_Proc
CEM_Pol ~~ CEM_Pract
CEM_Pol ~~ CEM_Proc
CEM_Pract ~~ CEM_Proc
'

# Fit model 
Fitted.Four.factor.multiple <- cfa(Four.factor.multiple, data = STP.data, std.lv = TRUE, ordered(c("CEM_Phil_1","CEM_Phil_2","CEM_Phil_3","CEM_Pol_1","CEM_Pol_2","CEM_Pol_3","CEM_Pol_4","CEM_Pol_5","CEM_Pract_1","CEM_Pract_2","CEM_Pract_3","CEM_Pract_4","CEM_Proc_1","CEM_Proc_2","CEM_Proc_PS_1","CEM_Proc_PS_2","CEM_Proc_HR_2","CEM_Proc_HR_3","CEM_Proc_OP_1","CEM_Proc_OP_2")))

# Summarize model and generate outputs
summary(Fitted.Four.factor.multiple, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, modindices = TRUE)
modificationindices(Fitted.Four.factor.multiple, sort. = TRUE)

However I received the following warning messages in lavaan:
In lav_object_post_check(object) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

On Wednesday, April 19, 2017 at 8:49:02 PM UTC+2, stefanie...@googlemail.com wrote:
Dear all,

I'm relatively new to lavaan and would greatly appreciate some advice on the following issue.
I ran a cfa model as follows:

# I use ordinal variables in Likert-scale lacking multivariate normal distribution - ordered and resulting robust estimation methods are recommended for such cases
# Define ordered(c(...)) as input for cfa
STP.data[,c("CEM_Phil_1","CEM_Phil_2","CEM_Phil_3","CEM_Pol_1","CEM_Pol_2","CEM_Pol_3","CEM_Pol_4","CEM_Pol_5","CEM_Pract_1","CEM_Pract_2","CEM_Pract_3","CEM_Pract_4","CEM_Proc_1","CEM_Proc_2","CEM_Proc_PS_1","CEM_Proc_PS_2","CEM_Proc_HR_2","CEM_Proc_HR_3","CEM_Proc_OP_1","CEM_Proc_OP_2")] <- lapply(STP.data[,c("CEM_Phil_1","CEM_Phil_2","CEM_Phil_3","CEM_Pol_1","CEM_Pol_2","CEM_Pol_3","CEM_Pol_4","CEM_Pol_5","CEM_Pract_1","CEM_Pract_2","CEM_Pract_3","CEM_Pract_4","CEM_Proc_1","CEM_Proc_2","CEM_Proc_PS_1","CEM_Proc_PS_2","CEM_Proc_HR_2","CEM_Proc_HR_3","CEM_Proc_OP_1","CEM_Proc_OP_2")], ordered)

# Define model, four-factor model with correlated factors, two variables (CEM_Proc_OP_1 and CEM_Proc_OP_2) freed to "load" on CEM_Proc and CEM_Pract
Four.factor.multiple <- '
CEM_Phil =~ CEM_Phil_1 + CEM_Phil_2 + CEM_Phil_3
CEM_Pol =~ CEM_Pol_1 + CEM_Pol_2 + CEM_Pol_3 + CEM_Pol_4 + CEM_Pol_5
CEM_Pract =~ CEM_Pract_1 + CEM_Pract_2 + CEM_Pract_3 + CEM_Pract_4 + CEM_Proc_OP_1 + CEM_Proc_OP_2
CEM_Proc =~ CEM_Proc_1 + CEM_Proc_2 + CEM_Proc_PS_1 + CEM_Proc_PS_2 + CEM_Proc_HR_2 + CEM_Proc_HR_3 + CEM_Proc_OP_1 + CEM_Proc_OP_2
CEM_Phil ~~ CEM_Pol
CEM_Phil ~~ CEM_Pract
CEM_Phil ~~ CEM_Proc
CEM_Pol ~~ CEM_Pract
CEM_Pol ~~ CEM_Proc
CEM_Pract ~~ CEM_Proc
'

# Fit model 
Fitted.Four.factor.multiple <- cfa(Four.factor.multiple, data = STP.data, std.lv = TRUE, ordered(c("CEM_Phil_1","CEM_Phil_2","CEM_Phil_3","CEM_Pol_1","CEM_Pol_2","CEM_Pol_3","CEM_Pol_4","CEM_Pol_5","CEM_Pract_1","CEM_Pract_2","CEM_Pract_3","CEM_Pract_4","CEM_Proc_1","CEM_Proc_2","CEM_Proc_PS_1","CEM_Proc_PS_2","CEM_Proc_HR_2","CEM_Proc_HR_3","CEM_Proc_OP_1","CEM_Proc_OP_2")))

# Summarize model and generate outputs
summary(Fitted.Four.factor.multiple, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, modindices = TRUE)
modificationindices(Fitted.Four.factor.multiple, sort. = TRUE)

Here are my questions:
1) It seems like CEM_Proc_OP_1 causes the warning. Is there any hint which I miss in the lavaan output telling me what I should do in order to get rid of the warning by re-specifying my model?

Not sure why that residual variance is negative.  It's not estimated due to categorical data, so you unfortunately can't apply the test in the Kolenikov and Bollen paper you linked to.  But maybe the factor loading is being over estimated to compensate for some model misspecification.  To see if CEM_Proc_OP_1 is more related to another variable(s) than the model accounts for, you can check the matrix of polychoric correlation residuals (differences between observed and model-implied polychoric correlations).

resid(Fitted.Four.factor.multiple, type = "cor")


2) estimates of paths between CEM_Proc_OP_1 / CEM_Proc_OP_2 and CEM_Pract / CEM_Processes are small and the absolute estimate of the factor correlation is close to 1.0. Knowing that, I would love to understand what I shall do now to counteract these issues. Could you please provide some advice?

From what I see, those factor loadings are huge (in absolute magnitude), not small.  But they are in opposite directions for the two factors.  Maybe a multicollinearity issue.  Try looking at the polychoric correlation matrix itself to see what the patterns of relationships are, which might reveal why those cross-loadings are so odd.

?lavCor

FYI, with 5 categories, you can probably trust the results if you treat them continuous with a non-normality correction (estimator = "mlr").  But since thresholds are pretty asymmetric for some items, estimates might be a little bit attenuated.

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

The matrix of polychoric correlation residuals did not reveal any other variables with which CEM_Proc_OP_1 would have medium or high correlations. In addition, I ran other models as well as an EFA. I found that I had to re-specify my model completely...

Best regards,
Stefanie
